events.summary: Moderna (MRNA) replaced Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) in the Nasdaq-100 before the open on Friday 2026-10-09, as Nasdaq announced on 2026-10-01. WBD left because it is being acquired by Paramount (Skydance); Reuters said on 10-01 the deal was expected to close on 2026-10-06 'following an extended delay'. Reuters put Moderna's value at about $75 billion after shares rose more than sixfold this year. Nasdaq says more than 200 products with more than $800 billion of assets track the index. The announcement is already in the news log's calendar. What is new here: the switch was due to take effect in this window, and the company it replaced was WBD. Moderna's weight in the index or in QQQM after it joined: not available. No published figure was found, and the latest holdings list (StockAnalysis, dated 2026-10-08) was published before the switch. Indirect sign that index funds bought: MRNA volume on Thursday 10-08 was 37,400,000 shares against 14,640,200 on Wednesday (data/prices/MRNA.csv). That fits index funds buying at Thursday's close (inference, medium). No source found confirms after the fact that the switch took effect. No source found reports a delay either.
events.why_it_matters: QQQM now holds a small slice of Moderna, which Santi also owns directly, so his Moderna exposure rises slightly. For QQQM's daily moves the effect is tiny, because a roughly $75 billion company is a small weight in an index led by NVIDIA (8.33%) and Apple (7.45%).

events.summary: Thursday 10-08: the Financial Times reported that OpenAI told investors its annualized revenue was 'approaching $50 billion at the end of September, rather than the $70 billion previously reported'. Benzinga/Yahoo said the gap came from different calculation methods, not lost sales, and that OpenAI declined to comment to the FT. Chip stocks sold off. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell as much as 4%. Arm, Intel and Marvell fell more than 6% and Micron more than 5% (Yahoo Finance live blog). Oracle fell more than 5% (Benzinga/Yahoo). Closes: Nasdaq Composite -1.25% to 27,193.34, S&P 500 -0.47% to 7,765.36, Dow +0.1% (+51.77) to 51,231.64 (Yahoo Finance/Motley Fool). From our price files: QQQM -1.31%, QQQ -1.34%, SPY -0.42%, chip fund SMH -2.84%, AMD -3.90%, TSM -3.01%. CNBC's headline that day: 'Nasdaq falls 1% as AI trade stumbles following OpenAI revenue setback' (page blocked, headline only). Attribution for QQQM: market -0.42 points, Nasdaq-100's extra move -0.91, the fund itself +0.02 (data/research/2026-10-09/thursday-attribution.json).
events.why_it_matters: This explains all of QQQM's -1.31%. It was not fund news. The index fell about three times as much as the S&P 500 because its biggest weights are AI chipmakers (NVIDIA 8.33%, Micron 4.84%, AMD 4.19%, Broadcom 2.57%, Intel 2.33%). It shows that QQQM carries the same AI-spending risk as Santi's single stocks, in milder form.

events.summary: University of Michigan, preliminary October reading released 10:00 a.m. ET Friday 10-09: consumer sentiment 46.3, down from 48.1 in September. Current conditions 44.7; expectations 47.3. Year-ahead inflation expectations 4.7%; long-run 3.5%. Director Joanne Hsu: 'Frustration over cost-of-living continues to mount, as consumers across the political spectrum believe that the trajectory of the economy has weakened since the beginning of the year.' Benzinga called it the second-lowest reading ever and the current-conditions index a record low (tier 3, not verified). Bloomberg headline: 'US Consumer Sentiment Falls to Five-Month Low in October'.
events.why_it_matters: Gloomy consumers and 4.7% expected inflation are a background risk for rates and spending. Stocks rose anyway on Friday.

why_chain.text: QQQM fell 1.31% on Thursday 10-08. QQQ fell 1.34% and the S&P 500 fund 0.42%. Split: market -0.42 points, the Nasdaq-100's extra move -0.91, the fund itself +0.02. So the cause was what the index holds, not the fund.

The Nasdaq-100 fell about three times as much as the S&P 500 because chip stocks sold off. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell as much as 4%; Arm, Intel and Marvell fell more than 6% and Micron more than 5%. From our price files: SMH -2.84%, AMD -3.90%, TSM -3.01%.
The trigger: the Financial Times reported that OpenAI told investors its annualized revenue was 'approaching $50 billion at the end of September, rather than the $70 billion previously reported'.
why_chain.evidence: https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/openai-revenue-20b-below-previous-181839907.html (tier 3, citing the FT); CNBC headline https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/07/stock-market-today-live-updates-.html (tier 2, headline only)

why_chain.text: Why that hits chipmakers: OpenAI is one of the biggest buyers of AI computing, mostly through cloud partners such as Microsoft and Oracle (Oracle fell more than 5%). If its revenue is lower, it may be harder for OpenAI to pay for the data centers it has promised to use. That would mean fewer chips ordered from NVIDIA, Micron, AMD and others, so investors lowered what they will pay for those companies' future profits.

It was not rates or the economy. The 10-year Treasury yield FELL from 5.28% to 5.22% (official Treasury data). Jobless claims were a low 197,000. On Wednesday rates were a candidate cause; on Thursday they were not.

Friday 10-09: QQQM +0.50%, QQQ +0.49%, S&P 500 fund +0.60%. Split: market +0.60, Nasdaq-100 extra -0.10, fund +0.01. Reporters credited easing oil and a tech rebound after a Bloomberg report that OpenAI expects to reach or exceed $70 billion in annualized revenue by year-end.
why_chain.evidence: data/metrics/attribution-2026-10-09.json; https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-friday-october-9-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-080148117.html (tier 3; the Bloomberg story itself was not opened)

products.name: QQQM (Invesco NASDAQ 100 ETF)
products.what_it_is: An exchange-traded fund that buys the roughly 100 largest non-financial companies on the Nasdaq exchange, in the same proportions as the Nasdaq-100 index.
products.analogy: A ready-made basket at the market: one price buys a small piece of about 100 big companies, weighted by size.
products.buyers: Individual and professional investors who want broad exposure to large US growth and technology companies in one trade.
products.how_it_works: Invesco holds the shares directly (physical replication) and adjusts them when Nasdaq changes the index. Example: buying Moderna and selling Warner Bros. Discovery for the 10-09 switch. Invesco earns 0.15% a year of assets.
products.price: 0.15% a year fee (P&I ETF data, as of 2026-10-06); QQQ, which tracks the same index, costs 0.18% (Invesco, as of 2026-06-30). Share price $309.39 at Friday's close (data/prices).

products.stage: Established, growing (net inflows over the past month).
products.size_for_company: not applicable (a fund, not a company); for Invesco the fee on $113.6 billion is about $170 million a year (our arithmetic: 0.15% x $113.6 billion; inference, not an Invesco figure)
products.competition: Invesco QQQ (same index, 0.18%); other Nasdaq-100 trackers (not checked in this window).
products.why_investors_care: Cheap, faithful tracking of the index is the whole product. Any fee rise or tracking gap would show here first.
products.watch_next: Invesco's updated holdings showing Moderna's weight; the Nasdaq-100 annual reconstitution (usually December; 2026 date not verified).

disconfirming_evidence.claim: An 'index fund' still behaves like an AI bet on a bad AI day: a single press report about OpenAI's revenue knocked the Nasdaq-100 down about 1.3%, three times the S&P 500's fall.
disconfirming_evidence.assessment: Valid and directly observed in the price data (QQQM -1.31% vs SPY -0.42%). It does not hit the draft triggers, but it supports the existing 'what I accept' risk: about 67% technology, about 47% in ten names, and about 28.7% in chip names in the visible top 25.

disconfirming_evidence.claim: Concentration warning: commentary says the Nasdaq rally depends on AI spending tied to a few buyers (OpenAI, Microsoft, Nvidia, Oracle). It claims about 70% of hyperscaler AI revenue comes from OpenAI and Anthropic.
disconfirming_evidence.assessment: Low-quality source (broker marketing commentary); its numbers are not verified and should not be cited as fact. The general risk it describes matches what happened on Thursday.

disconfirming_evidence.claim: QQQM's correlation with TSMC is close to the draft 'behaves like a tech stock' line.
disconfirming_evidence.assessment: 0.79 against a 0.8 trigger (TSM 0.79 on both 10-07 and 10-09). An early sign worth watching; not hit.

disconfirming_evidence.claim: The Motley Fool's Thursday wrap said Treasury yields 'surge[d]', with the 10-year rising to 5.28% at the close.
disconfirming_evidence.assessment: Contradicted by official Treasury data (10-year 5.22% on 10-08, down from 5.28% on 10-07) and by Yahoo (5.23%). The Fool figures look like Wednesday's (5.28% close, 5.35% intraday peak). Do not use them for Thursday.

disconfirming_evidence.claim: Friday's OpenAI 'rebound' story may not cancel Thursday's: the FT number (about $50 billion run rate at end-September) and the Bloomberg number (expects at least $70 billion by year-end) measure different things.
disconfirming_evidence.assessment: Unresolved. Chip stocks kept falling on Friday (SMH -0.65%), which suggests the market did not fully accept the reassurance (inference, low).
